title: merkle: CompletenessChecker error messages omit title/module and use tree key for project reqs
description:
spec/merkle/arch_completeness_checker.md specifies the contract for incomplete_change error output:

- message format cites the requirement title and module, e.g., "requirement 'Match changed nodes to beads' (impact) description changed but component NodeMatcher content leaf unchanged"
- `path` and `related` carry identity hashes — "the same values used everywhere else in the pipeline"

Actual code in merkle/completeness_checker.go deviates on two fronts:

1. Message format omits title and module: it emits only "requirement <hash> ... but component <name> content leaf unchanged". Readers can't tell which requirement is affected without reverse-lookup.

2. For project-level requirements, the `path` field carries the merkle tree key — SHA256("project/requirement/<id-hash>")[:12] — instead of the identity hash. Example encountered: path "1df4a31c4726" where the actual requirement identity hash is "58ea35f52b86" ("No runtime subprocesses"). The tree-key form matches nothing in spec files, forcing a double-hash reversal to diagnose.

Discovered during /spec authoring for proposal 2026-04-18-decouple-spex-from-br — mid-run completeness errors cited 1df4a31c4726; had to grep tree_builder.go to discover the double-hashing scheme before the violation could be pinpointed.

Fix:
- In checkAddedRequirement / checkModifiedRequirement / checkRemovedRequirement: expand the message to include the requirement title (looked up from the module spec) and the module name, per the spec example.
- In checkProjectRequirementModifiedOrAdded / checkProjectRequirementRemoved: use the underlying identity hash (projReqHash parameter) for the Path field instead of c.Path (which is the tree key in those call sites).

Tests: add a completeness-checker test asserting that path and related fields always carry an identity hash that appears in project.json or the relevant module.json.
close_reason: Reviewed and approved in PR#138. All review feedback addressed.

title: CompletenessChecker: project-req tree-key vs preq_id mismatch
description: CompletenessChecker compares the merkle tree key of a project requirement against module requirements' preq_id values, but these two identifier forms diverge. TreeBuilder keys project-requirement leaves as IdentityHash("project", "requirement", req.ID) (e.g. tree key 685919a2538b for a req whose req.ID in project.json is 13c15bc3c865). Module requirements store preq_id with the raw project-requirement ID (13c15bc3c865), not the tree key. In merkle/completeness_checker.go:266, findDerivedModuleRequirements compares req.PreqID == projReqHash where projReqHash = c.Path (the tree key). They never match for added or modified project requirements. Dormant until now because no prior PR added a new project-level requirement after TreeBuilder switched to the double-hash keying. First exposed by PR #128 (data flow contract layer), which adds project requirement 13c15bc3c865 Data flow contract layer. Diff reports: incomplete_change: no module requirement derives from project requirement 685919a2538b — false positive, since module requirement 81aac298ce04 in impact does derive from it via preq_id. Fix: translate the tree key back to the raw req.ID at the check boundary, or compute the tree key for each module req's preq_id when comparing in findDerivedModuleRequirements. Scope: merkle/completeness_checker.go and its tests. Should ship before PR #128 can complete its spex impact/apply run.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 27641af. findDerivedModuleRequirements now accepts both raw preq_id and tree-key forms so real-spec module requirements resolve their project requirement derivation correctly. Regression test TestREQ8_ProjectRequirement_Added_RawPreqIDDerivation added.

title: impact: BeadStatus never populated on mapping records, cleanup creates never fire
description:
impact req 3dcf3c279ac5 (Classify cleanup actions for removed nodes) says: a removed spec node with a closed bead must produce obsolete + cleanup create; open/in_progress produces obsolete only. ActionClassifier implements the rule at impact/action_classifier.go:118-128 by checking o.Record.BeadStatus == "closed". mapping.Record has the BeadStatus field (mapping/mapping_store.go:30).

Gap: BeadStatus is never populated on mapping records in production. impact.ReadBeads (impact/bead_reader.go) reads each bead's live status from br list --json into BeadSpec.Status, but cmd/spex/impact.go never calls ReadBeads and never merges BeadSpec.Status into Record.BeadStatus before handing records to MatchNodes. The field stays empty through the whole pipeline, so the closed-bead check at action_classifier.go:119 always evaluates false. No cleanup create has ever been emitted.

Dormant because no prior PR has removed a component whose bead was already closed. PR #128 (data flow contract layer) removes ProposalTagger — a closed bead — so this is the first case to exercise the path.

Fix: in cmd/spex/impact.go runImpactE, after store.List(), call impact.ReadBeads(ctx, beadBin) to get live statuses, build a map keyed by RecordID, and copy Status into each record's BeadStatus field before passing to MatchNodes. Add a --bead-cli flag (default "br") to the impact command so users can select the bead binary (mirrors apply). Tests cover closed, open, in_progress, and missing-bead cases.
close_reason: Cleanup creates now fire AND carry OldBeadID for lineage. ActionClassifier's orphan-handling path at impact/action_classifier.go:120-128 now sets OldBeadID=o.Record.BeadID on the cleanup Action, so BeadCreator emits --deps blocks:<old-bead-id> on the cleanup bead. An agent picking up a cleanup bead can now trace back to the obsoleted predecessor via br's dep graph instead of only by title. Regression test extends TestFR6_S5b_ClassifyActions_RemovedClosedBead to assert OldBeadID==spex-010 on the cleanup action.

comments.author: paalori
comments.text: Reopened: Plumbing works, but br list --json defaults to excluding closed beads. ReadBeads returns empty against a repo where all beads are closed (the common post-ship state), so cleanup creates still never fire. Need to pass --status filter to include all statuses when reading beads for impact classification.

comments.author: paalori

Cleanup creates now fire, but ActionClassifier does not populate OldBeadID on the cleanup Action (impact/action_classifier.go:120-127 sets only Type/Module/Node/NodeType/SpecNodeID/Reason — OldBeadID omitted). BeadCreator.createCleanupBead emits --deps blocks:<old-bead-id> only when action.OldBeadID is non-empty, so the lineage link between the cleanup bead and the obsoleted predecessor is silently dropped. title: impact: ActionClassifier leaves Action.Node as identity hash for added data_flows and test_sections
description:
spec/impact/arch_action_classifier.md defines Action.Node as the "affected spec node name" (line 63) and the reason-string templates (lines 80-84) use {node_name}, e.g.:

- "New spec node: {module}/{node_name}"
- "Code cleanup: {module}/{node_name}"

For MODIFIED nodes (matched branch), the code correctly resolves via nodeName(r) which reads r.Component from the mapping record. This works for components.

For ADDED nodes (unmatched branch), impact/action_classifier.go sets:

    node := u.Change.Path

where u.Change.Path is the identity hash, NOT the name. There is no lookup against the current spec graph to resolve the name.

Symptoms observed during apply for proposal 2026-04-18-decouple-spex-from-br:

- Component beads get proper titles: "emit: ChangesetBuilder", "ingest: Reconciler", "adapters: BrReferenceAdapter" (matched or component-only code path).
- Data_flow beads get hashes: "emit: dbe8d1e707d5", "ingest: 6fd1f0cbb76c", "adapters: 703128d3ebd6".
- Multi-component test_section beads get hashes: "emit: 280a5495eef8", "ingest: 2cd902e10873", "ingest: 2515c91337a5".

Reason strings are similarly affected: "New spec node: emit/dbe8d1e707d5" instead of "New spec node: emit/Emit flow".

Fix: in the unmatched branch of ClassifyActions (impact/action_classifier.go ~line 99, and similarly for orphaned/removed at ~line 137 if it uses u.Change.Path), use the `graph mapping.SpecGraph` parameter (already passed in) to resolve the spec node's name from the current module.json by (module, node_type, spec_node_id). Fall back to the identity hash only if the lookup fails (e.g., node truly not in current spec).

Suggested helper signature: `graph.NodeName(module, nodeType, specNodeID) string`.

Tests:
- A unit test that exercises ClassifyActions on an added data_flow and asserts Action.Node equals the data_flow's "name" field from module.json.
- Same for test_section.
- Same for component (regression: should still work).
close_reason: Fix verified via actual spex apply run in PR#111. impact/action_classifier.go:99 now resolves node names via new resolveNodeName helper over mapping.SpecGraph; tests TestClassifyActions_ResolvesAddedNodeNames and TestClassifyActions_ResolvesNodeName_NilGraphFallback added. Post-fix apply output confirms proper titles: emit: Emit flow, ingest: Ingest flow, adapters: Adapter flow, etc. — no more identity-hash fallbacks for added data_flows or test_sections.

title: Data reconciliation: .bead-map.json ghost records + broken deps post-21defea
description:
Commit 21defea (Apply data-flow-contract-layer: 7 created, 7 obsoleted) left the bead graph in an inconsistent state. Pure data fix — no spec or code change.

## Symptoms

### A. Ghost mapping records

Three records in .bead-map.json point to bead IDs that don't exist in the br DB:

- Record 18 (merkle/DiffCommand)     -> spexmachina-z9y (not found)
- Record 21 (impact/ActionClassifier) -> spexmachina-xl3 (not found)
- Record 29 (apply/ApplyCommand)      -> spexmachina-7nz (not found)

### B. Open predecessors for records 18, 21

The predecessors that were supposed to be obsoleted by 21defea are still open, labeled with the new proposal:

- spexmachina-ec7 (merkle/DiffCommand) — open, has spec_proposal:2026-04-12-data-flow-contract-layer + spex:18, missing spex:obsolete
- spexmachina-r4o (impact/ActionClassifier) — same pattern

These are the effective current beads despite the commit message claiming they were obsoleted.

### C. Gap at record 29

Predecessor spexmachina-tjs IS correctly closed. No open bead currently tracks apply/ApplyCommand.

### D. Broken spec-graph deps on new beads

All five new feature beads (7hb, p6z, lln, ec7, r4o) carry only lineage edges (blocks:<old-closed-id>). No spec-graph blocked-by edges wire them to each other. Root cause is a real impact->apply bug addressed at spec level in proposal 2026-04-18-decouple-spex-from-br.md; the data fallout lives today on the beads and has to be corrected manually.

## Fix plan

1. Reconcile mapping:
   - Record 18: bead_id z9y -> ec7
   - Record 21: bead_id xl3 -> r4o
   - Record 29: create new feature bead for apply/ApplyCommand, point record there

2. Wire correct spec-graph deps on open beads per spec/*/module.json uses and requires_module.

3. Test: every mapping record resolves to an existing bead; every new bead's dependency_count matches expected spec-graph edges.
